[Motif A — ROWAN CALL: D4-F#4-A4-B4-A4-F#4. In lilting 6/8, articulate three rising eighth-notes, sustain high B, then let A and F# fall and leave space. This belongs to the FIDDLE.]
[Opening: fiddle presents Motif A fully exposed with a real bow swell toward high B. No banjo or percussion in the opening.]
[Hearth reply: mountain dulcimer answers F#4-E4-D4; cello quietly presents the WORLD motif D4-A4-G4-E4-D4.]
[Gathering: upright bass establishes gentle 6/8 motion; mandolin adds short A4-E4-F#4-A4 fragments. Add low-mixed clawhammer banjo only as brushed rhythmic texture; it never states Motif A.]
[Horizon: fiddle reclaims the melody in the high register, doubled an octave lower by cello, with a soft viola inner harmony. Build through the bowing, not drums.]
[Coda: everyone drops away except fiddle and mountain dulcimer; Rowan Call followed by Hearth Answer; end on warm D resonance.]

source_prompt.style: Instrumental cinematic Appalachian chamber folk, lyrical old-time fiddle, acoustic post-minimalism, organic orchestral Americana; passionate close-miked solo fiddle is the unmistakable lead, with long legato bows, subtle double-stops, upward swells and natural slides. Resonant cello answers, mountain dulcimer drones softly, mandolin adds occasional syncopated replies, upright bass supports flowing 6/8; quiet low-mixed clawhammer banjo supplies only a soft brush-and-thumb backbeat. D Mixolydian, open fifths, warm suspended harmonies, subtle glass overtones, dark wide acoustic depth. Begin alone, build into interweaving chamber strings, reach one earned fiddle-led crest, finish intimately. Distinct warm humanity, no constant activity.

meaning_notes.text: That dip holds so much longing, yearning. But then that following peak arises and brings with it hope, continuance, perhaps some degree of strength even.
It is good, but by itself it is just okay. The portion before the peak makes it amazing.
Hope does not erase the longing. It arrives carrying it. Treat loss as a possible fictional reading, not fixed autobiography or canon.
